source.title: Problemas abiertos en series de Fourier de Jacobi-Sobolev

accepted.question_text: In the general theory of orthogonal polynomials defined by Sobolev inner products that may include derivative-evaluation terms, determine which analytic properties of standard orthogonal polynomials are preserved, what algebraic properties the new polynomials have, whether a parallel Hilbert-space operator theory exists, and which Pade approximants are associated with these polynomials and how those approximants behave.

For a general Sobolev orthogonality setting with two measures, determine the asymptotic behavior of the orthogonal polynomials when the supports of the measures do not coincide: in particular, when the supports are disjoint, or when they overlap but neither support contains the other. The known case is when the second measure is supported on the same compact set as the first; the unresolved task is to handle the non-nested or non-overlapping support cases where the algebraic relations available for the discrete Sobolev product are absent.

Let w be the classical Jacobi weight on [-1,1], dmu(x) = (1-x)^alpha (1+x)^beta dx with alpha,beta > -1, and define a discrete Sobolev-type inner product by <f,g> = integral f(x)g(x)dmu(x) plus the finite sum over k=1..K and i=0..N_k of M_{k,i} f^(i)(a_k) g^(i)(a_k), with mass points a_k in (-1,1) and nonnegative coefficients M_{k,i}. Establish upper estimates for the associated orthogonal polynomials, adapting the known exterior-mass-point Jacobi-Sobolev Fourier-series methods to the interior-mass setting where the Christoffel-Darboux formulas develop singularities at the mass points.

For a discrete Sobolev-type inner product built from the Jacobi measure on [-1,1] together with derivative-evaluation mass terms at the endpoints -1 and 1, develop the endpoint-mass case. In particular, determine estimates and related tools that would allow fourth-order boundary-value differential operators to be studied by Galerkin methods, and develop corresponding extensions of the Gauss-Lobatto quadrature formula for collocation methods using the modified Jacobi functional framework.
accepted.context_brief: Endpoint masses and fourth-order boundary problems

accepted.question_text: Let w(x)=h(x)(1-x)^alpha(1+x)^beta product_{j=1}^N |x-t_j|^gamma_j on [-1,1], where alpha,beta,gamma_j > -1, the points t_j are distinct points in (-1,1), h is continuous and positive on [-1,1], and the modulus of continuity condition w(h,delta) delta^(-1) is integrable on (0,2). For the discrete Sobolev-type inner product formed from w(x)dx and finitely many derivative-evaluation mass terms, extend the known upper estimates for orthogonal polynomials with generalized Jacobi weights to this Sobolev-type setting.
accepted.context_brief: Generalized Jacobi weights in Sobolev products

accepted.question_text: For Fourier-Sobolev series built from the orthogonal polynomials associated with a discrete Sobolev-type inner product using Jacobi or generalized Jacobi weights and interior mass points, determine natural uniform-convergence and mean-convergence results for the partial sums, in the spirit of known weighted norm inequalities for polynomial expansions associated with measures with mass points.
accepted.context_brief: Uniform and mean convergence of compact-support Fourier-Sobolev sums

accepted.question_text: For Laguerre-Sobolev-type orthogonal polynomials on an unbounded support, use the classical estimates for Laguerre polynomials to derive estimates for the Sobolev-type polynomials, distinguishing the case where the mass is located at the boundary of the support from the case where the mass is located in the positive real half-line. Also derive estimates for the corresponding kernels using the Sobolev extension of the Christoffel-Darboux formula.
accepted.context_brief: Laguerre-Sobolev estimates with mass location cases

accepted.question_text: For Fourier series with respect to orthogonal polynomials defined by the discrete Sobolev-type inner product with a single mass point at x=0, study mean convergence when the base measure mu is the Laguerre measure or the Hermite measure. Then determine how far such results can be extended to Freud measures dmu(x)=|x|^(alpha/2) exp(-|x|^beta) dx with alpha > -1 and beta > 0.
accepted.context_brief: Mean convergence for Laguerre, Hermite, and Freud Sobolev expansions

accepted.question_text: Consider the non-discrete Sobolev inner product <f,g> = integral f(x)g(x)dmu_0(x) + integral f'(x)g'(x)dmu_1(x). In the Jacobi-Sobolev case where mu_0=mu_1 is the Jacobi weight, let Q_n be the monic orthogonal polynomials for this inner product and let P_n^(alpha,beta) be the Jacobi polynomials. Determine whether estimates exist for Q_n and determine their order of magnitude relative to P_n^(alpha,beta), taking into account the known finite relation Q_n + a_n Q_{n-1} + b_n Q_{n-2} = P_n^(alpha,beta) + c_n P_{n-1}^(alpha,beta) + d_n P_{n-2}^(alpha,beta).
accepted.context_brief: Magnitude estimates for non-discrete Jacobi-Sobolev polynomials

accepted.question_text: For the Jacobi-Sobolev polynomials Q_n in the non-discrete Sobolev inner product with two continuous measures, obtain estimates for the kernel L_n(x,y)=sum_{k=0}^n Q_k^*(x)Q_k^*(y), where Q_k^* is the orthonormal sequence corresponding to Q_k.
accepted.context_brief: Kernel estimates for non-discrete Jacobi-Sobolev polynomials

accepted.question_text: For Fourier expansions in Jacobi-Sobolev polynomials associated with the non-discrete Sobolev inner product with two continuous measures, obtain estimates for the nth Fourier partial sums and analyze whether the Fourier projection operator is bounded with respect to the Jacobi-Sobolev norm.
accepted.context_brief: Partial sums and projection boundedness in Jacobi-Sobolev norm
